title: City life 4
note: B2 vocab leaf, drafted 2026-09-05 on the home lane. Three predecessors own 94 words between them — a1_places (30), a1_places_2 (30) and a2_town (34) — covering the map of a town, how you move around it and every building on it, down to roundabout, crossroads, pavement, cashpoint and litter bin. None of that is repeated. The corrected sweep also caught two words from THIS LANE'S OWN morning: infrastructure and homelessness, both taught by leaf_society_b2, whose node is still `coming`. Fourth unit running where the corrected pool has caught a self-collision the shipped tool would have missed. So this unit is the city as a thing that is planned, argued about and lived in rather than navigated: how it looks and what it offers (urban, district, inner city, high-rise, skyline, riverside, green space, venue, nightlife, amenity), how it moves and jams (congestion, rush hour, commuter, ring road, bypass, cycle lane, pedestrianised, noise pollution, overcrowded, sprawl), and who decides and who pays (resident, council, planning permission, regeneration, affordable housing, derelict, run-down, vibrant). C57 card 0 recaps Town 1-3. C49 all 36 across three boards of 12. Build-the-family: reside -> residence -> resident is a three-form thread inside the unit, plus congestion from congested and regeneration. E10 Use is rewrite production; every underline reconstructs its answer.

cards.title: You already know
cards.note: Town 1, 2 and 3 gave you the map and how to cross it — city, street, square, station, bank, museum, bus, tram, left, right, opposite, roundabout, traffic lights, crossing, pavement, car park, shopping centre, suburb, outskirts, neighbourhood. Those words carry the sentences here. What is new is the city as something people plan, argue about and complain about, not something you walk across.
cards.note_cz: Town 1, 2 a 3 ti daly mapu a jak po ní chodit — city, street, square, station, bank, museum, bus, tram, left, right, opposite, roundabout, traffic lights, crossing, pavement, car park, shopping centre, suburb, outskirts, neighbourhood. Ta slova nesou zdejší věty. Nové je město jako něco, co lidé plánují, o čem se hádají a na co si stěžují — ne něco, čím jen projdeš.

points: One verb here builds two nouns — the place and the person.
**-ence** gives the place, **-ent** gives the person.
